translation_en: Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah, including these hadiths: The Messenger of Allah said, “Were it not for the Children of Israel, food would not spoil and meat would not putrefy; and were it not for Eve, no female would ever betray her husband.”

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi said: I read to Malik ibn Anas, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating during the time of the Messenger of Allah. Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the Messenger of Allah about it, and the Messenger of Allah said, “Tell him to take her back, then leave her until she becomes pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure. After that, if he wishes, he may keep her, and if he wishes, he may divorce her before having intercourse with her. That is the waiting period for which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded that women be divorced.”

Yahya ibn Yahya, Qutaybah, and Ibn Rumh narrated to us; these are Yahya’s words. Qutaybah said: Layth narrated to us. The other two said: al-Layth ibn Sa‘d informed us, from Nafi, from Abdullah, that he divorced one of his wives once while she was menstruating. The Messenger of Allah ordered him to take her back and keep her until she became pure, then menstruated once more while with him, then wait until she became pure from that menstruation. If he wished to divorce her, he should do so when she was pure, before having intercourse with her. That is the waiting period for which Allah commanded that women be divorced. Ibn Rumh adds in his report: When Abdullah was asked about that, he would say to a man, “If you divorced your wife once or twice, the Messenger of Allah commanded me to do this. But if you divorced her three times, she is forbidden to you until she marries another husband, and you have disobeyed Allah regarding how He commanded you to divorce your wife.” Muslim said: al-Layth gave a precise wording when he said “once.”

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, who said: I divorced my wife during the time of the Messenger of Allah while she was menstruating. Umar told the Messenger of Allah about it, and he said, “Tell him to take her back, then leave her until she becomes pure, then menstruates once more. When she becomes pure, let him divorce her before having intercourse with her, or keep her. That is the waiting period for which Allah commanded that women be divorced.” Ubaydullah said: I asked Nafi, “What happened to that divorce?” He said, “It counted as one.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated this to us: They said: Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from Ubaydullah, with this chain and a similar report, but he did not mention Ubaydullah’s question to Nafi. Ibn al-Muthanna’s report says, “Let him take her back”; Abu Bakr’s says, “Let him return her.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ismail narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi, that Ibn Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar asked the Prophet, who ordered him to return her, then wait until she menstruated again, then wait until she became pure, and then divorce her before touching her. That is the waiting period for which Allah commanded that women be divorced. Ibn Umar, when asked about a man divorcing his wife while she was menstruating, would say, “If you divorced her once or twice, the Messenger of Allah ordered me to return her, wait until she menstruated once more, then wait until she became pure, and then divorce her before touching her. But if you divorced her three times, you have disobeyed your Lord in what He commanded you concerning divorce, and she is separated from you.”

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Muhammad—Ibn Akhi al-Zuhri—narrated to us, from his uncle: Salim ibn Abdullah informed us that Abdullah ibn Umar said: I divorced my wife while she was menstruating. Umar told the Prophet, and the Messenger of Allah became angry, then said, “Tell him to take her back until she has a future menstrual period, separate from the period during which he divorced her. If he then decides to divorce her, let him do so while she is pure from menstruation and before having intercourse with her. That is divorce in the proper waiting period, as Allah commanded.” Abdullah had divorced her once; it was counted as one of her divorces, and Abdullah took her back as the Messenger of Allah had ordered him.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated this to me: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih informed us: Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us: al-Zubaydi narrated to me, from al-Zuhri, with this chain, except that Ibn Umar said, “I took her back and counted the divorce I had given her.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Numayr narrated to us; these are Abu Bakr’s words. They said: Waki‘ narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, the freedman of the family of Talhah, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar told the Prophet, who said, “Tell him to take her back, then divorce her while she is pure or pregnant.”

Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Hakim al-Awdi narrated to me: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us: Sulayman—Ibn Bilal—narrated to me: Abdullah ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Ibn Umar, that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar asked the Messenger of Allah about it, and he said, “Tell him to take her back until she becomes pure, then menstruates once more, then becomes pure; after that, he may divorce her or keep her.”

Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa‘di narrated to me: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, who said: For twenty years, trustworthy people told me that Ibn Umar had divorced his wife three times while she was menstruating and was ordered to take her back. I neither suspected them nor knew the hadith until I met Abu Ghallab Yunus ibn Jubayr al-Bahili, a reliable man. He told me that he asked Ibn Umar, who told him that he had divorced his wife once while she was menstruating and was ordered to return her. I asked, “Did it count against him?” He replied, “What else? Or was he incapable and foolish?”
Abu al-Rabi and Qutaybah narrated this to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, with this chain and a similar report, except that it says: Umar asked the Prophet, who ordered him.

Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to us: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather, from Ayyub, with this chain. The report says that Umar asked the Prophet about it, and he ordered him to take her back until he divorced her while she was pure and without having intercourse. He said, “Let him divorce her at the beginning of her waiting period.”

Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to me, from Ibn Ulayyah, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Yunus ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn Umar, “A man divorced his wife while she was menstruating.” He said, “Do you know Abdullah ibn Umar? He divorced his wife while she was menstruating, and Umar went to the Prophet and asked him. He ordered him to take her back and then begin her waiting period anew.” I asked him, “When a man divorces his wife while she is menstruating, does that divorce count?” He said, “What else? Or was he incapable and foolish?”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us. Ibn al-Muthanna said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: I heard Yunus ibn Jubayr say: I heard Ibn Umar say: I divorced my wife while she was menstruating. Umar went to the Prophet and told him about it. The Prophet said, “Let him take her back. When she becomes pure, if he wishes, let him divorce her.” I asked Ibn Umar, “Did you count that divorce?” He said, “What would prevent it? What do you think if he was incapable and foolish?”

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Khalid ibn Abdullah informed us, from Abd al-Malik, from Anas ibn Sirin, who said: I asked Ibn Umar about the wife he had divorced. He said, “I divorced her while she was menstruating. This was mentioned to Umar, who mentioned it to the Prophet. He said, ‘Tell him to take her back; when she becomes pure, let him divorce her while she is pure.’” He said: So I took her back, then divorced her while she was pure. I asked, “Did you count the divorce you gave her while she was menstruating?” He said, “What would prevent me from counting it, even though I was incapable and foolish?”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us. Ibn al-Muthanna said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Sirin, who heard Ibn Umar say: I divorced my wife while she was menstruating. Umar went to the Prophet and informed him. He said, “Tell him to take her back; then, when she is pure, let him divorce her.” I asked Ibn Umar, “Did you count that divorce?” He said, “What else?”

Yahya ibn Habib narrated this to me: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us. Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated this to me: Bahz narrated to us. Both said: Shu‘bah narrated to us with this chain, except that their report says, “Let him return her.” In both reports, it says: I asked him, “Do you count it?” He said, “What else?”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Ibn Tawus informed me, from his father, that he heard Ibn Umar being asked about a man who divorced his wife while she was menstruating. He said, “Do you know Abdullah ibn Umar?” The man said, “Yes.” He said, “He divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar went to the Prophet and told him what happened, and he ordered him to take her back.” The narrator said: I did not hear him add anything beyond that to his father.

Harun ibn Abdullah narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayman, the freedman of Azza, ask Ibn Umar, while Abu al-Zubayr listened: “What do you think about a man who divorces his wife while she is menstruating?” He said: “Ibn Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating during the time of the Messenger of Allah. Umar asked the Messenger of Allah and said, ‘Abdullah ibn Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating.’ The Prophet said to him, ‘Let him take her back.’ He returned her, and said, ‘When she becomes pure, let him divorce her or keep her.’” Ibn Umar said: The Prophet recited, “O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period.”
Harun ibn Abdullah narrated to me: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Ibn Umar, with a similar account.

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated this to me: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayman, the freedman of Urwah, ask Ibn Umar, while Abu al-Zubayr listened, with a report like Hajjaj’s and some additional wording. Muslim said: He was mistaken in saying “the freedman of Urwah”; rather, he was the freedman of Azza.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us; these are Ibn Rafi’s words. Ishaq said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us. Ibn Rafi said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: During the time of the Messenger of Allah and Abu Bakr, and for two years of Umar’s caliphate, a triple divorce was counted as one. Umar ibn al-Khattab said, “People have hastened in a matter in which they had been given time. If only we enforced it upon them.” So he enforced it upon them.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Rawh ibn Ubadah informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us. Ibn Rafi narrated to us—these are his words: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Ibn Tawus informed me, from his father, that Abu al-Sahba said to Ibn Abbas, “Do you know that a triple divorce used to be counted as one during the time of the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and the first three years of Umar’s rule?” Ibn Abbas said, “Yes.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, from Tawus, that Abu al-Sahba said to Ibn Abbas, “Tell me something you know: was a triple divorce counted as one during the time of the Messenger of Allah and Abu Bakr?” He said, “That was so. When it was Umar’s time, people began issuing divorces repeatedly, so he enforced them upon them.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Hisham—Ibn Dastawa’i—who said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir wrote to me, relating from Ya‘la ibn Hakim, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who used to say regarding declaring one’s wife forbidden: “It is an oath for which expiation is due.” Ibn Abbas said, “Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example” Quran 33:21.

Yahya ibn Bishr al-Hariri narrated to us: Muawiyah—Ibn Sallam—narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir: Ya‘la ibn Hakim informed him that Sa‘id ibn Jubayr informed him that he heard Ibn Abbas say: “When a man declares his wife forbidden to him, it is an oath for which he must make expiation.” He said, “Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example” Quran 33:21.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Ata informed me that he heard Ubayd ibn Umayr report that he heard Aishah say: The Prophet used to stay with Zaynab bint Jahsh and drink honey at her home. Hafsah and I agreed that whichever of us the Prophet entered upon first would say, “I smell maghafir on you. Did you eat maghafir?” He entered upon one of them, and she said that to him. He replied, “No, I drank honey at Zaynab bint Jahsh’s, but I will not do it again.” Then this was revealed: “Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?” through “if you both repent” Quran 66:1–4, concerning Aishah and Hafsah; and “When the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives” Quran 66:3, referring to his words, “No, I drank honey.”

Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-Ala, and Harun ibn Abdullah narrated to us: They said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah liked sweets and honey. After the Asr prayer, he would visit his wives and draw near to them. He went to Hafsah and stayed with her longer than usual. I asked about it, and someone told me that a woman from her people had given her a skin of honey and she had served the Messenger of Allah a drink from it. I said, “By Allah, we will devise a plan for him.” I mentioned this to Sawdah and said, “When he comes to you, he will draw near to you. Say to him, ‘Messenger of Allah, did you eat maghafir?’ He will say no. Then say, ‘What is this smell?’ The Messenger of Allah strongly disliked having an odor detected from him. He will tell you, ‘Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.’ Then say, ‘The bees must have fed on urfut.’ I will say the same to him, and you, Safiyyah, say it too.” When he came to Sawdah, she said, “Sawdah says: By the One besides whom there is no god, I almost began saying what you told me while he was at the door, out of fear of you.” When the Messenger of Allah drew near, she said, “Messenger of Allah, did you eat maghafir?” He said, “No.” She said, “Then what is this smell?” He said, “Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.” She said, “The bees must have fed on urfut.” When he came to me, I said the same to him. Then he came to Safiyyah, and she said the same. When he came to Hafsah, she said, “Messenger of Allah, shall I give you some of it to drink?” He said, “I have no need of it.” Sawdah said, “Glory be to Allah! By Allah, we have deprived him of it.” I said to her, “Be quiet.”

Abu Ishaq Ibrahim said: Al-Hasan ibn Bishr ibn al-Qasim narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, with exactly this report. Suwayd ibn Sa‘id narrated this to me: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, with this chain and a similar report.
